summary: Peter Adamson is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1994–2000). He held posts at King's College London (~2000) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979 and completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen (-2004) under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include the University of Edinburgh (2005–2010) and Leiden University (2010).

Peter Connolly is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University. In 1980, he held a post as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester.

Peter D. Hershock works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied at Yale, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and under traditional teachers Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim and Seungsahn Haengwon. He held posts at the East-West Center.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Oxford, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Walpola Rahula.

Peter Edwin Hook is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Pennsylvania (~1967–1973), and served as Professor Emeritus of Linguistics and Indo-Aryan Languages at the University of Michigan (~1973–2008).

Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, and traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche. He held a post at Deakin University (attested 1994).

Peter Flügel is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (attested 1996), SOAS University of London as Chair of the Centre of Jaina Studies (attested 2006–2017), and the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 2022).

Peter Francis Kornicki works in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Oxford and studying in Tokyo and Kyoto. He held academic posts at the University of Tasmania, Kyoto University, and the University of Cambridge (~1985–2014).

Peter Friedlander is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at SOAS (1983–1991). He held positions at the Wellcome Trust, La Trobe University (attested 1996–2010), and the Australian National University (2013).

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1948–1952). He held professorships at Utrecht University (1965–1975) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–2003).
Peter Gerlitz (1926–2013) was a religious studies scholar. He studied under Friedrich Heiler (~1950–1954) and held an academic post at the University of Bremen (~1974–1991).

Peter Giles (1860–1935) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Aberdeen, Cambridge, Freiburg, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and John Peile. He held posts at Emmanuel College from 1887 and served as Cambridge's Reader in Comparative Philology from 1891.

Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the London School of Economics (-1990) and held an adjunct post at Adams State University (attested 2007).

Peter Hartmann (1923–1984) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Münster under Alfred Schmitt (~1948–1950), later serving as professor at Münster (from 1956) and the University of Konstanz (1969).

Peter Harvey is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Sunderland (1976–2011), where he became Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies, and co-founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996.
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a graduate student at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.
Peter J. Claus is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who held posts at California State University, East Bay (attested 1996) and California State University (attested 1997).

Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) earned his Ph.D. from Yale University. He held teaching posts at Yale (~1960–1964), Vassar College, the University of Washington (~1965–1970), Bennington College (~1970–1971), and the University of Otago (~1971–1998).
